comments.builds: Measured on the dump (Donkey Kong Bananza.nup: base v0, update v458752 = 3.2.0, add-on content 040074a01bf13001): nx2/dump.py reported the program id and main's build id (sdk 18265dae..., SDK and NVN 20.5.19, no subsdk modules), nx2/nup.py the update's version, and nx2/lift.py's image line put main at 0x80020000. Its ExeFS is byte-identical to dkb-pc-recomp's dkb458752 target, whose 3.2.0 addresses therefore apply to this lift unchanged.
comments.profile: Empty on purpose until measured, as a number that looks right is worse than none: patch modules (none needed to play the tunnel), gfx (the frame limiter: HOS_FPS_LOG once its module is known), upscale (program keys, from RX_VK_SHADER_CENSUS), hooks (gfx_clock: HOS_TICK_LOG lists GetSystemTick's callers).
comments.profile.video_catchup: The guide movies' player counts every picture it submitted: one the catch-up skips is never handed back, and the player aborts at its loop's flush (main+0xe1ada0 from 0x8189b900; with skips, after 1-2 loops).
comments.profile.graphics_scale: Bananza sizes its render targets by GetCurrentGraphicsScale's enum (main 0x8033e9b4 / 0x80569324 keep it as a mode byte, 0x803ad180 / 0x805695d0 index a float table {3, 12, 16} with it): with the host's 1 it drew at 80% of its 2880x1620 (2304x1296; scenes 1536x864 / 1676x943), with 0 at the full size (2880x1620; 1920x1080 / 2095x1179)
comments.released: In the release: its own tile in RecompLauncher (recomplauncher.json games[]), its own copy asked for (inputs[]), which the builder checks against this profile's build id (make_game.py --game-<key>)
